summary: Lunar Mission Planner is an AI-powered lunar mission planning platform designed to make Moon exploration smarter and safer. It uses NASA's JPL Horizons and Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LOLA) elevation data to analyze solar illumination, lunar terrain, energy conditions, and communication visibility at potential landing locations. Its interactive lunar map and mission analysis dashboard help users understand environmental conditions and assess mission feasibility. The integrated Super Intelligent System (SIS) provides AI-powered text and voice interaction, making complex scientific results easier to understand for both researchers and the public. By transforming NASA's open space data into accessible mission insights, Lunar Mission Planner aims to support safer rover operations and more informed lunar exploration.
details:
Lunar Mission Planner — See the Moon Before You Explore It

Lunar Mission Planner is an AI-powered platform designed to help researchers and mission planners assess potential lunar rover exploration areas before a mission begins. Lunar missions face challenges such as extreme and changing sunlight, hazardous terrain, craters, limited energy, and communication constraints. Our project brings relevant lunar data and mission insights together in one interactive platform.

What does it do and how does it work?

Users can enter a potential lunar landing location using its latitude and longitude, along with the mission date and time. The platform uses NASA's JPL Horizons system to obtain relevant Sun and Earth position information and elevation data from the Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA), aboard NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) to examine the surrounding lunar terrain.

It presents mission-related information through an interactive lunar map and analysis dashboard, helping users understand sunlight conditions, terrain characteristics, and communication visibility. The platform also considers energy-related factors relevant to rover planning. Its integrated Super Intelligent System (SIS) provides an AI-powered assistant that users can interact with through text and voice to better understand the results.

What are the benefits and intended impact?

The platform makes complex scientific information easier to access and interpret. It can help users identify potential environmental challenges, compare mission conditions, and make more informed planning decisions. Our intended impact is to support safer, more efficient, and better-informed lunar exploration, particularly for rover missions operating in challenging regions such as the lunar south pole.

What tools and technologies did we use?

Our software was developed using Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Python. We integrated NASA's JPL Horizons data and LOLA lunar elevation data. For the conversational AI system, we used LiveKit Agents and Google's Gemini AI, with LiveKit supporting real-time text and voice interaction.

The project is a software platform; no custom hardware was required for its development.

How is the project creative?

Our main innovation is bringing lunar scientific data, interactive mission visualization, and a conversational AI assistant together in one planning platform. Instead of requiring users to interpret separate scientific datasets independently, SIS helps explain the information in an accessible way through both text and voice. This combines data-driven exploration planning with an intuitive human-AI interface.

What factors did our team consider?

We considered the changing illumination conditions on the Moon, surrounding elevation and terrain hazards, crater-related risks, rover energy requirements, communication visibility, and the influence of mission date and time. We also considered data availability, scientific accuracy, and the need to communicate uncertainty clearly. Lunar Mission Planner is intended as a decision-support tool to assist mission planning, not as a replacement for professional mission validation or safety certification.
